Team / Claire — reviewed Acumen's redline and drafted suggested compromise language. Key points and suggested replacements below (see attached RI-suggested-language_20260815.docx for full text):

1) Output ownership / derivative language (replace Section 8.2):
> Original (Acumen ask): "Customer Output and derivatives thereof shall remain the sole and exclusive property of Customer and Provider shall have no rights to use, exploit, sell or otherwise commercialize Customer Output or any derivative works."

Proposed (Redwood compromise): "Customer Output and any Derivative Works that contain identifiable Customer Content shall remain Customer's Confidential Information and subject to Customer's IP ownership. Provider may retain non-identifiable aggregate performance metrics and anonymized usage statistics for the sole purpose of improving service quality, provided such data cannot be reverse-engineered to reconstruct Customer Content."

Rationale: preserves customer's ownership while allowing Redwood to safely measure product performance.

2) Training / feedback license and lockbox (new Section 9.4):
- Option A (Customer opts out): Provider will not use Customer Content or Customer Output to train models, and will delete request-level logs within 30 days unless Customer expressly opts into longer retention via written Order Form.
- Option B (Customer opts in): If Customer opts-in, Provider will store and use content for training only within a segregated, access-controlled training environment (a "lockbox"). Any such use will be governed by: (i) duration of retention specified in Order Form; (ii) restricted access list; (iii) no downstream commercial licensing without additional agreement.

Ask: Claire, does Acumen prefer Option A (strict opt-out) or Option B (controlled lockbox) for the initial rollout? Procurement timeline suggests a quick decision.

3) Telemetry and debug logs: propose 30-day default retention, 90 days with opt-in for extended troubleshooting. We can add a 3rd-party SOC2 statement and KMS/HSM key controls into the appendix if Acumen requires more technical assurances.

Next steps: if Claire confirms Option A vs B, we'll turn the doc into a redline and get legal to finalize. If Option B, Grace can scope the lockbox deployment (cost/ops).

Thanks Ben — and thanks Priyom for coordinating.

Acumen will accept the Proposed (Redwood compromise) wording for Section 8.2 with one small tweak: replace the phrase "non-identifiable aggregate performance metrics" with "aggregate system metrics that do not contain Customer Content or Customer Output and cannot be re-identified to Customer or end users." That change is to be explicit about re-identification risk.

On retention: we'll go with Option B (controlled lockbox). Requirements:
- Lockbox access limited to named Redwood engineers and audited quarterly;
- Retention and use limited to model-safety and quality improvements for 12 months unless further extended by mutual written agreement;
- Any datasets used for model retraining must be reviewed by Acumen and certified as de-identified prior to use.

If you can incorporate those bullets into the wording and return a final redline, procurement will circulate the Order Form for signature. DocuSign link to follow once we have the final doc.
